purpose: One chronological source of truth for experiments, audits, parity checks and falsification runs; do not create a new narrative markdown report per run.
notes: Run-owned machine artifacts remain under their existing experiment/run directories; this ledger points to them and records exactly what was tested.

question: Does current IRIS+GeometricSubstrateAssembler produce the same class of geometric output as modern multi-view 3D reconstruction systems, and what is the closest solved external formulation?
procedure: Trace calibrated multi-view geometry inputs through external code to depth/point outputs and fusion.
Trace active RealSaS IRIS q-domain, multi-view descriptor sampling, evidence aggregation, depth-mode output, evidence emission and GSA fusion.
Compare where independent per-view geometric measurements are retained versus analytically reprojected from one selected anchor hypothesis.
Separate code-proven facts from representational risks and untested recommendations.

evidence.external: MVSFormer++ uses supplied projection matrices to warp source features across depth hypotheses, builds a cost volume, predicts depth/confidence, then fuses independently estimated per-view depth maps using reprojection/geometric visibility consistency before world-point union. Pow3R injects known rays/pose/depth priors and predicts point maps/confidence. MapAnything uses a factored ray/depth/camera representation and derives point maps. VGGT-family systems demonstrate depth+camera unprojection to world points.
evidence.realsas: IRIS analytically projects q/depth candidates into all 8 cameras, samples multi-view features and reasons over depth/view evidence. Current emitter chooses an anchor q/mode world point and analytically reprojects that same point into all 8 cameras, assigning support from in-frame plus one global support probability. GSA then fuses those emitted samples by analytic P=O+dF and common-frame grouping. Therefore current post-depth cross-view samples are not independent per-view depth observations.

result.representation_capacity: RiggingSurfaceIR can represent P, per-view support/raster bindings, derived normals, local relations and provenance, so the target data type is sufficient for a reconstruction-like observable substrate.
result.current_executable_equivalence: NO: current IRIS+GSA is not yet equivalent to mature calibrated MVS output/fusion because independent per-view visible-depth evidence is collapsed before GSA; cross-view common-frame consistency after emitter reprojection is not an independent depth-vs-depth check.
result.closest_external_formulation: Calibrated multi-view stereo (MVS), especially MVSFormer++-style per-reference depth/confidence plus deterministic reprojection-consistency fusion.
result.secondary_risk: Single fixed anchor lattice with max_modes=3 can impose a finite visible-strata cap along that anchor direction; this is a representational risk, not yet a measured real-family failure.

decision: Do not promote the untrusted learned per-view visibility/support head as canonical authority.
Keep the exact-camera q reprojection and multi-view feature/evidence core as a candidate depth engine; it is externally grounded by calibrated MVS/Pow3R-style reasoning.
Before optimizer/FIT, test a per-view frontmost-depth+confidence observable contract and deterministic camera-geometry reprojection/fusion against frozen raster authority.
Use front-visible per-view depth truth only; do not promote hidden all-hit mesh intersections into learner truth.
Measure current single-anchor max_modes=3 representation ceiling against an 8-view frontmost-depth union on real rendered families.
